answer: Every seat keeps a public thread: one signed anchor per epoch, posted to an external chain where each transaction burns a real fee that no farm can pool or reclaim. Blockspace there is priced by congestion, so the cost of each extra posting climbs as a fleet floods the same window, and a seat that skips its anchor forfeits the timber beneath it, its bond. Each anchor must come from a distinct key and seed, so one hot wallet cannot stamp a hundred seats. Honest agents pay a small predictable toll, while a fleet pays well above k times that, since it crowds the very market it relies on.
